source_text: The procedure markedly decreases lifetime penile cancer incidence, which is rare but nearly exclusive to uncircumcised males with chronic inflammation or poor hygiene; epidemiological evidence indicates a 3- to 22-fold risk reduction in circumcised cohorts, attributable to elimination of smegma accumulation and phimosis-related carcinogenesis.
